chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no charity (sadaqah) nor emancipation (itq) except what is intended by it is the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.وَجْهُ اللَّهِ: The Face of Allah (meaning for His sake alone)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for charity and emancipation to be valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the validity of charity (sadaqah) and manumission (itq) hinges on the intention being exclusively for Allah's sake, excluding worldly motives like social prestige. This hadith underscores the Shia principle that the spiritual efficacy of financial acts of worship is contingent upon pure sincerity (ikhlas), a concept deeply rooted in the jurisprudential discussions of al-Kafi regarding the conditions of valid transactions.
